subject: VPC/On-Prem Ops Readiness + Air-Gapped Checklist

Subject: RFP follow-up: VPC / On-prem checklist and air-gapped options

Hi Laura,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement and security here at Tarmond are preparing our final vendor pack and would like a short, actionable operations readiness checklist for your private deployment options (VPC, on-prem, and fully air-gapped).

Specifically we need:

- Clarification on KMS/HSM integration (local vs managed keys)
- How audit logs and access logs are stored and retained in private deployments
- Any limitations for fully air-gapped installs (patching, model updates)

If possible, could you send a one-page checklist plus a mapping to our standard security controls? We have a doc deadline Monday 4 Aug.

Appreciate it — I can loop in our InfoSec contact if helpful.

Regards,

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com

Subject: RE: RFP follow-up: VPC / On-prem checklist and air-gapped options

Laura / team — draft checklist attached. Key technical notes below (summarized):

1) Installer & upgrades
- On-prem deploy: Helm + operator behavior for K8s, or systemd package for VM installs.
- VPC (customer AWS/Azure/GCP): deployment uses customer-managed subnets and secure egress rules; images pulled from our signed registry into a private ECR/GCR repo.
- Air-gapped: we provide a signed, hashed artifact bundle (offline_install.tar.gz) delivered via secure transfer (SFTP or physical media). Install includes SHA256 checks and vendor GPG signature verification.
- Upgrades for air-gapped installs: offline upgrade bundles can be applied; we recommend quarterly bundles. Emergency patches available as signed hotfix bundles.

2) Keys & cryptography
- KMS integration: supports customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault) or our hosted KMS.
- HSM: we support HSM-backed keys via PKCS#11 interface; for fully air-gapped customers keys remain local to HSM—no private key material leaves customer boundary.

3) Logs & telemetry
- Audit logs: by default sent to customer-managed S3 or Blob storage; alternatively to local syslog or a Splunk/ELK endpoint.
- Sensitive telemetry (usage aggregates) can be disabled for private deployments. For compliance, we retain only what customer permits.

4) Model lifecycle and updates
- Model binaries: can be packaged into offline bundles for air-gapped installs or pulled from customer-curated registry in VPC mode.
- We sign model artifacts; integrity checks are enforced during load time.

5) Operational boundaries
- Redwood provides the control plane for hosted customers. For private deployments, we offer an optional local control plane (no outbound) or a hybrid model with customer-approved egress endpoints for telemetry.

Attached: redwood_vpc_onprem_checklist_v1.pdf, redwood_airgap_install_instructions.txt, redwood_network_diagram_vpc.png

Let me know any missing items before Laura consolidates.

-Karthik
Principal Solutions Architect

Adding a few operational clarifications for the checklist:
- Support model: Standard business-hours support is included; enterprise SLA adds 24x7 on-call and response time commitments.
- Maintenance windows: for VPC/on-prem we recommend a weekly 2-hour maintenance window for non-critical upgrades; emergency hotfixes can be scheduled outside window with prior notice.
- Runbook: we will supply a runbook and automated health-check scripts to validate KV cache health, model load times, and latency baselines after an upgrade.

I also noted a procurement ask about acceptance testing: recommend we include a short acceptance test suite (smoke tests + perf sample) in the checklist.

-MC
Senior Customer Engineering Manager

Andrew — attaching the one-page ops readiness checklist and a controls mapping workbook as requested. Also included a short note on air-gapped installer and a redacted link to our SOC2 report.

In brief:
- We support customer-managed KMS and HSMs; keys can be provisioned and kept local to your HSM (PKCS#11).
- Audit logs can be delivered to your S3 bucket or local syslog endpoint; retention is configurable per account.
- Air-gapped installs are supported via signed offline bundles; upgrades require application of a signed bundle. Emergency hotfixes are delivered as signed patches.
- Acceptance testing: we include a smoke/perf suite in the bundle and recommend a 72-hour validation window before cutover.

Thanks Laura — package looks great. Two quick clarifications before we circulate internally: 
1) HSM locality: when you say "keys remain local to HSM," can you confirm that no key material or unencrypted key metadata is transmitted to Redwood control plane in hybrid mode?
2) Audit logs retention: we need to ensure logs are immutable for 1 year and accessible to our SIEM (Splunk). Can you confirm export formats and whether timestamping is preserved?

If you can confirm these two points we can move to contracting.

Thanks,
Andrew
Procurement | Tarmond Health

From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: Andrew Liu <andrew.liu@tarmond.com>
Cc: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: VPC/On-prem ops readiness package (Tarmond Health)

Andrew — quick answers: 
1) HSM locality: confirmed — when configured to use customer HSM (PKCS#11), private key material never leaves the HSM. In hybrid control-plane configurations we only exchange key identifiers and policy metadata; no unencrypted key material or raw private keys are transmitted. We can provide an architecture note and PKCS#11 integration checklist if you want.

2) Audit logs: we support JSON and syslog formats, and deliver immutable object storage via customer-managed S3 with object-lock if required. Timestamps are preserved (ISO8601 UTC) and we include sequence IDs for event ordering. We also support streaming to Splunk/HTTP Event Collector.

Hannah, please attach the controls mapping extract that shows the KMS/HSM and logging coverage for SOC2.

Laura

[Sent from Redwood]
